16 A cylinder contains a fixed mass of gas. The gas, at a constant pressure of 1.3 × 105
Pa, expands
from a volume of 900 cm3 to a volume of 1100 cm3.
What is the work done by the gas during this expansion?
A
26 J
B
130 J
C
2600 J
D
13 000 J

hints: Notice the gas expands at constant pressure from $900 \text{ cm}^3$ to $1100 \text{ cm}^3$, so first find the increase $\Delta V$ in $\text{cm}^3$.
Recall work done by a gas at constant pressure is $W = p\Delta V$, but $p$ in $\text{Pa}$ needs $\Delta V$ in $\text{m}^3$ with $1 \text{ cm}^3 = 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$.
Convert your $200 \text{ cm}^3$ increase to $\text{m}^3$ and multiply by $1.3 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ to get $W$ in $\text{J}$.
walkthrough: Identify the change in volume: $\Delta V = 1100 - 900 = 200 \text{ cm}^3$.
State the rule for constant pressure expansion: $W = p\Delta V$.
Convert the volume change to SI units: $\Delta V = 200 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3 = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$.
Calculate: $W = 26 \text{ J}$, with $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^3 = \text{J}$, and positive because the gas expands and does work. This is option A.

B.explanation: This value is 5 times too large and results from an error in the $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$ conversion for the $200 \text{ cm}^3$ change.

C.explanation: This uses the volume change in $\text{cm}^3$ without converting to $\text{m}^3$, giving $1.3 \times 10^5 \times 0.02$ incorrectly.

D.explanation: This multiplies pressure by a volume in $\text{cm}^3$ directly, ignoring the $10^{-6}$ factor to reach $\text{m}^3$.
